name: מְנַשֶּׁה
gloss: making forget, one who makes forget
summary: Joseph's firstborn by Asenath, born in Egypt, and the tribe from him, whose host marched under Gamaliel son of Pedahzur (Num 10:23); also the king of Judah, Hezekiah's son, and two men of Ezra's day. The name is the piel participle of נָשָׁה “forget”, and Joseph gives the reason himself: “God has made me forget (נַשַּׁנִי) all my toil and all my father's house” (Gen 41:51). The name tells what God did for Joseph in Egypt, as his second son Ephraim's tells that God made him fruitful there (Gen 41:52).

evidence.note: “Joseph called the name of the firstborn מְנַשֶּׁה, for ‘God נַשַּׁנִי all my toil and all my father's house’.”
The second son Ephraim, “for God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction”: both names are what God did.
“Over the host of the tribe of the sons of מְנַשֶּׁה, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.”
Jacob crosses his hands, setting Ephraim before Manasseh the firstborn.
Manasseh son of Hezekiah reigns in his place.
A Manasseh among the sons of Pahath-moab who had taken foreign wives; another at Ezr 10:33.
The same verb in the niphal: “Israel, you will not be forgotten by me.”
Μανασσῆ among the twelve tribes sealed.

note: BDB m.cp.aj is the name (146 tokens), m.cp.ak the gentilic מְנַשִּׁי “Manassite”, which TIPNR folds into Manasseh@Gen.41.51. Jdg 18:30 reads מְנַשֶּׁה with a raised נ, where the consonants are משה; TIPNR assigns that verse to Moses@Exo.2.10, so he is not tagged here, though the token may sit under m.cp.aj. The tribe and its land are covered by the person record of Joseph's son.
